Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric This LEATHER LAPTOP MESSENGER BAG FOR MEN (by Leather Centric) is made of real leather--animal hide, NOT the man-made “pleather” stuff that’s often marketed on Amazon as “real leather” or “genuine leather”. That’s a big plus, but the bag itself has a lot of minuses.

First, the bag’s styling is so old-fashioned, it makes the bag look cheap. You have to really love the 1950s “retro” look, to like the overall appearance. The bag definitely looks handmade, but it also looks crudely rustic.

Second, although the bag has lots of zippered compartments (inside and outside), it is only 3” deep. It has no expansion gussets, so the total capacity is one laptop or one very thick sheaf of documents. Internal zipper compartments are relatively useless if a bag can’t expand to hold the things added to the compartments.

Third, the bag is difficult to open. It opens with two metal clasps--these are hidden beneath the purely decorative buckled front straps. You have to pull up on both clasps at once to lift the flap, and you can’t do this easily without laying the bag flat on one side, or holding it on your lap. The leather flap itself is very stiff (at least when the bag is new), and this adds to the opening difficulty.

Fourth, the bag has no locking mechanism. Not that it is easy to open (see previous paragraph).

Fifth, the brass fittings must tarnish very easily, because the bag arrives with every single exposed brass piece wrapped tightly in thin plastic wrap. It takes something very sharp to cut the plastic, and you must be careful not to scratch the fittings. (I succeeded in removing the wrappings without damaging the bag, but I punctured my left wrist with an Olfa knife in the process.)

The bag is reasonably priced (about $90 on Amazon). It comes with a snap-on shoulder carrying strap, and has a sturdy, permanently attached satchel handle. The handle is very comfortable. The bag leather is already distressed, so you needn’t worry about scratches. This is a truly rugged laptop bag.
text_fidelity_b: Leather Laptop Messenger Bag for Men - Handmade Laptop Briefcase Satchel by Leather Centric

MOMAX Portable 56” 1.87lbs Compact Aluminum Alloy Lightweight Camera Tripod Monopod with Swivel Head, 5.5 lbs Loads for Phone, Camera Sony Canon Nikon, Travelling, Learning and Working (Grey) The MOMAX Compact Aluminum Tripod is super compact, moderately sturdy, and fairly light-weight and I really love it.

I have three kinds of tripods, all consumer grade, nothing professional. As seen in my pictures, I compare the size of all three types. Farthest to the right is the standard tripod that doesn't fold down all that much, the middle is the compact tripod with a ball head and quick release, and the MOMAX is the farthest left.

From the pictures, you can see how much more compact the MOMAX tripod is. What you can't see is that due to its compact size, the footprint when fully deployed is also much smaller. It expands to a height of 56 inches, which is about chin or head height, which is tall enough for most portraits.

The MOMAX tripod is super portable while not compromising on stability and sturdiness. Its folded size is only 10.3" long and 3" in diameter. Compare this to my previous solution, which was to use a monopod/selfie stick with a small tripod at the bottom, this tripod is so much better. Mounting my mirrorless camera on the MOMAX, I don't worry about the whole thing falling over.

The only tiny complaint I have about this tripod is its mounting head. It is a ball joint with a 1/4" thread at the top. It can't be removed easily to be replaced with a better solution and there is no quick-release option.

Each of my tripods serve a purpose but I foresee using the MOMAX most often because most of the time.
text_fidelity_b: MOMAX Portable 56” 1.87lbs Compact Aluminum Alloy Lightweight Camera Tripod Monopod with Swivel Head, 5.5 lbs Loads for Phone, Camera Sony Canon Nikon, Travelling, Learning and Working (Grey)

text_fidelity_a:
SquareTrade 4-year Office Protection Plan Purchased this 4 year plan in November 2016 on a Dell Laser Printer. Thus the printer was a little over 2 years when it started doing weird things and I made a claim.

Basically ... the printer stopped printing black ... it just got lighter and lighter. I attempted to clean the heads and change the cartridges to no avail. The printer would also keep running and not stop after done doing a printer job.

I printed my receipt / invoice off Amazon to PDF. I then went to SquareTrade's website attached the receipt. I then made a claim. The claim process was pretty easy and they actually approved me for a full refund. I just needed to fill out an affidavit. I did this but a week later I still had no refund. Somehow my affidavit didn't get logged even though I got a confirmation email. I called them on the telephone and they fixed everything and were kind about it. Within 24 hours they emailed me an Amazon gift certificate (my choice) which gave me an additional 5% back. I this received a $121 refund on an $118 printer that died in its 3rd year.

I have no complaints and would purchase a square trade warranty again.

Bits of interest as I read other people's low reviews:

1) You purchase a 4 year warranty, but really, for example, it is just 3 extra years beyond the purchase's original 1 year warranty (or however long applies). If your item dies in a year, you have to go to the manufacturer for help.

2) You need to have your receipt. No biggie. Amazon is super amazing that way. I can see all my order back to when Amazon just sold books. Print the invoice / receipt to PDF and there you go. Receipt. Proof of purchase.

3) There is no paper copy of this plan. This is great. It saves trees. You would probably lose it anyway. But Amazon also kept a copy of the fact that I purchased this along with the printer. It was in my order history. There is your proof and all the telephone numbers are there. It is so easy. You don't need a stack of papers.

4) If you file a claim and get 100% of your purchase price back, you cannot file a claim for the same item again. No brainer.

5) This isn't accident insurance. If you do a dumb thing like leave your camera on top of your husband's big rig fender and it ends up in a million pieces 1/2 mile from your house ... it is NOT covered. If you think it should be ... well then ... Take out an insurance policy ... not a warranty. Those are two different things.

6) If you got a deal and paid $65 for your item, but the item now sells for $400 ... you still only paid $65 and $65 is all you are getting back. You don't make money off warranties.
text_fidelity_b: SquareTrade 4-year Office Protection Plan

EVEO Premium Vinyl Record Cleaner Kit - Complete 4-in-1 Vinyl Records Cleaning Kit for Records Albums-Includes Soft Velvet Record Brush,Cleaning Liquid,Duster &Turntable Stylus Cleaning Gel Wifey has a vast collection of vinyl. She has about 200 albums stored in her player cabinet and only God knows how many more, stored in large plastic totes. A lot of these albums are rare and collectable, fetching big money on the vinyl trading market. We will sit in her office/nest talk, and just listen to music.

There is something about music recorded on vinyl. No, it's not the best medium for the purest sound. But, it DOES have a quality to it that has been lost to all the new tech out there. It's warm, rich and even the little pops and clicks you hear from well worn records is somehow comforting.

This little record cleaning kit helps us preserve the quality of the records and the music on them. It's simple, easy to use and worth every penny. We clean every record before we play it. And, using the included gel, we clean the stylus at the beginning of every session. Good purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair) My old G930 ear pads were flaking like crazy after several years of daily, all-day use, and I was hesitant to buy these at first because several people said they were too small. But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

PHOTOS:
I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.
text_fidelity_b: iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair)

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Express - HD Streaming Player I will come back and do a further review when all the Christmas/New Year's hoopla is out of the way, but my husband got interested when he saw this gadget arrive in the mail and spent around an hour installing it (most of the hour spent trying to find somewhere to plug it in). He said installation is baby simple--plug it in the TV, plug in the power cord, then follow the instructions on the screen. You will need a computer, a tablet, or a smartphone to do the setup. However, I am automatically subtracting one point off the final rating because, although Roku states during the setup that there are many places you can access through its gadget for free, you are REQUIRED to give it a credit card number in order for your registration to complete "just in case" you want to order something that costs money in the future. This is like saying you can't surf Amazon and pick out a couple of books without registering first. I'd say you should allow your customers to "cross that bridge" when they come to it, not force them to supply a credit card, especially since Roku stresses in their advertising that there is no subscription cost!

Update: April 2017...I have taken this Roku stick off our guest room television and put it on the main TV because it gets Britbox, which I signed up for today. I am really happy with it, but must warn that the stick itself must be in plain view of the remote and you must aim the remote directly at it or it won't respond. Otherwise there is great reception and the remote is very easy to use. I found some interesting looking channels including one for the Great Courses.

Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold) This folding keyboard is a bit of a betwixt and between product, but if it is the sort of thing you think you might use, then it’s got a lot to like about it. If you have a tablet (and my experience is with iPads so keep that in mind), then their built in keyboard is a better choice for short work just because it’s larger and more natural to type. For longer work, the choice will be more individual in that some people hate writing for extended time on the hard surface of a tablet keyboard and others don’t mind at all. I can do a pretty long stint and for really long work, I’ll shift over to a Bluetooth keyboard, either Apple’s own or a smaller Logitech one that also acts as a cover. I’d prefer both of those to this because again, they are larger and so more comfortable.

When one considers the keyboard as a phone accessory, then things change a bit, and this become a much more viable choice. If I have to do any halfway extensive typing on a phone for work (something beyond texting, an email or two, etc., then this would definitely be my preference over the phone itself.

1) it takes up very little space (and comes with a nice little pouch). Tossing it into a backpack is nothing, but I could easily fit it into a coat pocket, a cargo pants-like pocket, keep it in my car console without it blocking much space. None of which would be true for my wireless Apple keyboard or even my slimmer Logitech one. The additional “bulk” is therefore relatively negligible.

2) the typing is quite nice on it. I was pleasantly surprised at the key travel, the ease, the tactile sense.

3) It’s definitely small and a little cramped, but not so I notice it unless I’m typing for a long time (half hour or more) and then I just need to take a few minutes break. The small size doesn’t come into play too often. I had to readjust to the apostrophe, and one has to hunt and seek a bit for less-used keys, but that’s easy enough and once you’ve been typing for a while it becomes just as second nature as normal typing does. And it’s much faster and much more comfortable than extensive phone typing

4) the stand is a nice little touch that works quite well, placing the phone at a usable and pleasant working angle and letting you sue it in both portrait and landscape mode.

5) I haven’t exhausted the battery so can’t speak to how long it will go, but it’s certainly lasted a good number of hours, more than I’d ever use it for (if I’m working that long I’m going to my laptop or tablet)

6). Build quality seems sufficient. I wouldn’t say it feels highly durable, but nor would I call it cheap feeling or overly flimsy. And when it’s folded I have no concerns about it breaking.

All in all this was actually quite the pleasant surprise and again, if you would ever find yourself needing to use your phone for that sort of mid-range work (more than you’d want to do on a phone keyboard but not so much you’re turning to a laptop) then I’d highly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Foldable Bluetooth Keyboard, Geyes Folding Wireless Keyboard with Portable Pocket Size, Aluminum Alloy Housing, Carrying Pouch, for iPad, iPhone, and More Tablets, Laptops and Smartphones(Gold)

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Fortunately I bought this at a much cheaper price at $16 instead of the current price as of this writing at $27. There are lots of comparable wireless vertical ergonomic mice less than $27 that also include recharging and cool LED lights. Although it's a decent ergonomic vertical mouse, there are some legitimate gripes with this mouse after months of use so now I'm looking to try a different brand of vertical mouse.

The 2.4Ghz range is pretty bad. I found this out later down the road when I had to switch the USB dongle to a port on the back of my computer. At first I thought my batteries were low (or some dirt interfering with optical sensor) because my mouse cursor would stagger on and off as a moved cursor across screen. That was really frustrating not only for browsing but games. When I put the dongle closer to the front of computer it worked much better.

Now onto the batteries. This may be good or bad depending on preference but it uses AAA batteries. Although replacing batteries seems like an inconvenience, if you have a mouse with a built-in rechargeable lithium ion battery and the batteries go bad or defective then you would have to trash the whole mouse instead of just replacing the batteries.

There is a separate top button on the mouse for DPI toggle (800/1200/1600) but I can't tell what mode it is in unless I move the mouse across the screen every time I toggle it so it is kind of inconvenient. Would be nice so you can visually see the dpi on the mouse or on screen.

Overall, the mouse feel good upon touching it. The texture on the mouse is not glossy plastic but has a slight comfy texture on it. My personal gripe with the ergonomics is it feels a bit narrow and the hand does not feel relaxed. I think the culprit is the thumb rest position feels like it is a bit upwards causes your thumb to squeeze inward instead of relaxing. So I try not to point or put my thumb in the default thumb rest but more below the thumb rest or even slight bend my thumb so it's not straight and stiff.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

Conversely: 1 = much worse than expected. 2 = worse than expected. This New Stars Scale thus allows a negative rating as some have complained that they "Can't give negative 5 stars." Well now you can as 1 and 2 are in effect negative ratings, being lower than 3 which is essentially "OK. It works as expected, no better, no worse."

Well this mouse gets a New Stars Scale rating of only 2 because there is no way by glancing at it to tell if it is on or off. Rather one has to either 1) wiggle the mouse and see on the computer screen - if it is up and running - what the cursor does, or even if it is there or 2) pick up the mouse and look at the tiny black on/off switch on the bottom. Whether on or off, the tracking beam is invisible to the human eye.

Whereas my Amazon Basics mouse has a red jewel on top that lights up when it is on. Good idea! And it has a solid feel and better click. It is better then expected (or normal) so it gets a 4.

Tera Grand - Apple MFi Certified Lightning to Headphone Jack Audio Adapter, Durable Flexible Super Soft PVC Jacket iPhone 14/13/12/11 Pro Pro Max Plus Mini SE XS XR X 8/7/6, iPad Pro Air This is the first aftermarket dongle for lightening to 1/8" jack where the inline mic works as well as controls. I was amazed by this. What's much more impressive is that the fidelity of these DAC is outstanding and I experience much less distortion across the the full dynamic range on 15Ω dual-driver headphones from as low as 7 Hz. In fact, they performed flawlessly where other expensive amplifiers which no mic headphone controls (only the amps own buttons) worked at all. The Apple dongle doesn't really do a good job with larger headphone drivers which is why so many people get in line amps for their expensive earbuds. So
far, I’ve yet to try an in-line amp that’s worth what I paid for it. This guy is $20 and it does the job much better. I will never buy an Apple dongle or in-line "amplifier" again for an iPhone X series where there is no jack. This is clearly the way to go. Granted, there is no way to charge and have this control at the same time, but I guess this is a problem with the MFI spec from Apple. It's crappy, but no fault of this vendor. (It’d be great if Apple could be less thick about thinks like this and realize that people don’t always want to use a charge pad. It’s so silly.)

The design of this dongle is super rugged and I have not had any issues with distortion or phone problems. It seems just as reliable as the Apple dongle on an iPhone XS Max at minimum. I'm buying a couple more just to have them around since I hate not having my dongle nearby. (Tee-hee.) I’d just rather not have to pay the dongle tax to Apple anymore. They do wear out.

Also, I highly recommend the ERJIGO KZ ZS6 earbuds: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0756WVBZ9 as they pair incredibly with this dongle even at high volumes. I couldn’t believe that they sounded better on this than a fancy in-line amp! They sound as good or better than my UE Triple Fi 10's on the standard Apple dongle! For a total spend of $70 you are getting your money's worth and then some! Note, the fit of the Triple Fi is definitely superior to pretty much any earbud made, not to mention their noise-blocking capabilities. I doubt anyone will beat them there, but they are discontinued. (Thanks, Logitech.)

text_fidelity_a:
Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu I benchmarked using 3DMark, Time spy. From the results you can see it falls about where you would expect for its hardware and pricepoint. You are going to do better than an entry level gaming laptop, but you aren't going to be blowing anyone out of the water. But... this comp isn't really made for high performance.

It did handle both Minecraft and Ark. If you have kids you may have run into issues with Minecraft being RAM greedy, which is why you want at least 8GB and this has 16GB. So it will handle it with most mods pretty well.

Ark is terrible on computers. Even high end gaming rigs can struggle with it. It is one of the reasons I used it for testing. It is so poorly optimized that it will crash your PC and chuckle at your demise. This computer handled it well on medium settings, which isn't too bad. I wouldn't run epic settings on anything short of a NASA computer, and even still I'd be worried it would crash the space station or accidentally launch missiles.

Bottomline; this computer will make most games playable, they will not be "epic". It's a decent entry level gaming computer. I am not going to tell you to build your own if you want to save money and get a better set up for the same amount. Honestly, if you were of the mindset to do that you would not be considering $700 Dell computers. I have built my own computer, I have also wanted to throw it on the lawn and light it on fire, because when something goes wrong I have no one to blame but myself, and no one to fix it either. So... ignore the "build it yourself" shamers. You do you. If you want to buy an entry level gaming computer go for it. I would strongly recommend saving up the additional $250 to get the upgraded version of this computer though. For not much more, you get a whole heck of a lot more computer. Better processor, better graphic card, way better storage, and an SSD to run your operating system.

I knocked a star for the price and because the driver update software they have on there is a joke. I had to go manually update drivers myself. If that's not your deal I recommend adding a 3rd party driver updater, do not rely on Dells. If you are feeling brave you can buy a more powerful gaming computer for $700, you will just have to do a bit more research that they are a legitimate company.
text_fidelity_b: Dell Inspiron Gaming PC Desktop AMD Ryzen 7 2700 Processor, 16GB DRAM, 1TB HDD, AMD Radeon RX 580 4GB GDDR5 Graphics Card, Windows 10 64-bit, Blue LED, Model Number: i5676-A696Blu

I bought this because it was a fashion statement for my Red Hat years, albeit an expensive one. It is a gorgeous shade of nail laquer red with antique gold lettering on the keyboard. The keys remind me of Chinese ceramic tiles. It is not as light as I thought it would be, but it is light enough to keep in my purse without feeling the extra weight. It has Win XP and starts up fast. The wireless LAN found a connection instantly. It has very little software so you won't waste much time getting rid of what you don't want. I understand that when "designer" is added to anything, it ups the price, but this could be a little cheaper. I wish it came with the matching mouse. It does come with a shiny red satin bag, which I don't care for because it's too gaudy for my taste. HP brought down the price of the matching tote bag and scarf, however. Get noticed!

03/09 Update
I just ordered the matching mouse from Beach Audio through Amazon-expensive but it completes the set. HP doesn't carry it and doesn't plan to according to the response I got from them. I just received the matching tote and scarf from HP. I like the scarf but not the tote. The tote is canvas and quite sturdy-plenty of room in the separate slot for the computer, extra battery and the mouse. But the large floral design is not to my taste. It was half price when I ordered it so I will keep it. I may learn to like it.

BTW, the photo above shows the additional black battery that can be ordered. The original battery is red, like the computer.

Srhythm NC35 Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.0, Fast Charge Over-Ear Lightweight Headset with Microphones,Mega Bass 50+ Hours’ Playtime I want to point out up front, for those who are afraid these will be too big for a small head, that they fit me fine. I have a small head. I am a short woman, I have little ears, a little head. When these headphones are adjusted to be fully contracted, even without doing any bending of the top part, they fit great. They are lightweight but substantial, very comfortable, and I can see myself listening to them for hours without discomfort. I can lean back in my recliner without anything touching the headphones.

I didn’t know about the whole thing about burning in headphones. I’ve spent the last few hours down that rabbit hole, with all the opinions pro and con, etc., and I’m glad I’m doing it because I can already tell the headphones are responding to the burn-in process. I went to Spotify and looked for burn-in playlists, and I’m playing through one of them now.

I will not use these for noise cancelling, so I cannot comment on that. I want headphones that don’t bother my ears during hours of listening, that give me a clean, clear experience of the dynamics of the music, and that seem to become a part of me. So far, these are doing that. When I first started listening, I could tell these headphones were a little stiff and muddy, but they are loosening up now and becoming quite wonderful. I’m very pleased. And I’m only a few hours into the burning in.

Update: I just tried the ANC button. I’m sitting here, still in burn-in, watching the news on TV and periodically checking in to be sure the burn-in playlist is still playing. I could hear the TV when I was listening to Alice in Chains, and then I turned on the noise cancelling/ANC switch. Hey, this noise cancelling works pretty good! Of course, you get more pressure in your ears with ANC turned on, so it’s not a mode I would listen in for very long, but it definitely cancels the noise. Can’t hear a thing from the TV now. Flip the ANC switch, and I hear the TV. Flip it again, and there’s no voices coming through from the TV.
text_fidelity_b: Srhythm NC35 Noise Cancelling Headphones Wireless Bluetooth 5.0, Fast Charge Over-Ear Lightweight Headset with Microphones,Mega Bass 50+ Hours’ Playtime

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix Z90 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 5x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch Touch-Screen LCD (Red) The Fujifilm FinePix Z90 is a great point and shoot camera. It comes in a variety of colors, but I like the bright red finish of the camera I have. The design is unique from other cameras - it resembles a wallet or envelope. To turn the camera on, you simply slide the lens cover down; this is the part of the camera that looks like an envelope flap. Some of the options are a little harder to use than other small cameras, but the available features are worth a little time to learn to use.

Besides the stylish design, I like the many innovative features of the camera. For example, it's very easy to switch from playback to camera mode with the buttons on the camera. Once in playback mode, I found the functionality to have many more options compared to other similar cameras. You can compare photos side-by-side or with the press of an on-screen button, you can display thumbnails of several photos at once.

There are too many features to describe each one in detail, but below is a summary of my favorites:
* Good picture quality for size and type of camera
* Many settings manageable by touching the screen
* Robust playback mode
* Includes lithium ion battery and charger
* Ability to take one photo without flash and immediately take same picture with flash and compare results side-by-side (Great for taking an initial photo to test lighting conditions)
* Can load photos to PC even without the included software using standard windows functionality
* In Playback mode, can go to Menu and select specific photo. Then when photos are loaded to the PC, only those selected photos will be uploaded to Facebook.
* Zoom in/out easily by touching a round button on top of the camera - easier to get to and use than the bars on other cameras that must be tapped on one end or the other to zoom in and out
* Can select a mode that allows a photo to be taken by touching the screen instead of the shutter button
* When turning the camera vertically to take a picture, the menu options are automatically displayed in a portrait mode so they are easy to read

Overall, this camera has several unique, up-to-date features that are surprising, especially for a camera at this price point. The stylish design makes it a great choice for adults or teens. Facebook and YouTube users will appreciate the technology making is easier than ever to post photos and video clips. If you're looking for a small camera with a fun design and new features, the FinePix is worth a second look.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix Z90 14 MP Digital Camera with Fujinon 5x Wide Angle Optical Zoom Lens and 3-Inch Touch-Screen LCD (Red)

text_fidelity_a:
VideoSecu Low Profile TV Wall Mount Bracket for Most 32" - 75" LCD LED UHD Plasma HDTV, Compatible with Sony Bravia Samsung LG Haier Vizio Sharp AQUOS Westinghouse Pioneer ProScan Toshiba 1NN The bracket is incredible! I used it on a Samsung Plasma 60 inch ,(600x400-Vesa) PN60F5500. At first I was a little wary. The plasma is 2013 model ,weighs by itself about 60 pounds.Its solid, and the weight of my TV held it down without using security brackets. You need at least an 18 inch long screw driver because you cannot reach behind it once installed. A few turns and you're set. I found it easier to unscrew , first tighten , then go in the opposite direction so it locks the screwdriver in the center making it easier to remove. I left it untighten, since it held in place without them.

Im not a professional installer (like drilling holes and finding a stud in the wall) but was able to use my old screws from the wall to install this mount from my older plasma.. I did however have to drill 2 more at the bottom because of the Vesa difference. Beyond that, everything else was simple.Its solid once installed, very easy, and simple to understand.

CON: Personal pet peeve. The only con is on 60 inch TVs you cannot reach behind easily to use the security brackets.You have to use an 18 inch long screw driver or similar size to tighten them. (booklet does not say this . Only says use a screwdriver)They are not needed because the weight of the TV holds in in place. In my opinion, I like to do everything by the instructions. Not tighten the security brackets made me feel like I skipped a step. I will say its stays in place, and does not move, jiggle etc. Lifting the bottom of a 60 inch is not easy, so there is no worry about it being easily done, even by a kid since the hooks are on the top. Other reviewers have said security brackets are not needed to hold it in place. I just left them barely connected so I could have the option to screw on later.

PS: If you own a 60 inch and im guessing 65 (max size), it will not look like the picture after adding the back portions on the TV. At first I was under the impression it would not work, but adjusted the height on the TV brackets and it fit barely, but did fit.It does work on a (600x400) vesa mount TV.
text_fidelity_b: VideoSecu Low Profile TV Wall Mount Bracket for Most 32" - 75" LCD LED UHD Plasma HDTV, Compatible with Sony Bravia Samsung LG Haier Vizio Sharp AQUOS Westinghouse Pioneer ProScan Toshiba 1NN

Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black The KONNEK STEIN True Wireless Earbuds are a decent set of wireless earbuds. The sound quality is good, I’ve been using them with music and streaming shows, and I haven’t been disappointed with the sound quality.

I’m not as pleased with the short battery life, touch controls, and lack of audio cues.

I get about 2-3 hours of playback per charge. It’s rare for me to battery drain earbuds, but with this pair, I hear the low battery chime every time I use them.

The touch controls and lack of audio cues go together. The touch controls are super easy to activate on accident. More than once I’ve taken the earbuds out only to find I hit Play while doing so, and they kept playing music. I also activate random controls when adjusting the earbuds in my ears … and I don’t always know what I’ve done. Did I turn ANC on or off? The audio cues are just beeps, not an announcement like “ANC on/ANC off.”

I like the design of the case. It has a sliding top, so you can actually clean the entire area where the earbuds sit. When you put the earbuds inside the case, a light flashes to show their battery level. The case charges wirelessly or via USB-C. There’s only one LED light on the outside of the case, it’s easy to miss when you’re trying to see if the case is charging or not.
text_fidelity_b: Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black

text_fidelity_a:
1/2Mile Solar Driveway Alarm System-Up to 70FT Wide Sensor Range 3 Adjustable Sensitivities-Fully Weatherproof Outdoor Motion Sensor&Detector DIY Security Alert System I have been working out of detached workshop behind my house & set this in front of my house to capture the circular drive. It's not excessively far but it's out of range for a bluetooth device reach. It rings if anything goes through the circle (where the Camaro is) or down the drive past the house. I have tested it by walking at the very edge of the drive & it hasn't failed to alert. I may adjust the settings down before I move the receiver inside because it picks up a lot of cat activity. I didn't realize how many neighborhood cats stroll through my drive early in the morning.
I wanted to check this out before I committed to a mounting place so I set it under that oak tree. I thought it might be too shady to maintain the solar power requirements but it's been there a week with no issues. It's so discrete I'll probably just keep it on the rocks & move it closer to the tree. The mounting hardware is pretty nice, though, with a ball-jointed mount that sets up easy since it comes apart & has a lot of adjustment.
The receiver has three or 4 chimes & none of them are subtle. It also has another 30 or so songs. Some are holiday themed which could be fun if you were expecting guests for a party. It has some public domain tunes from the Baroque & Renaissance period as well as some contemporary tunes like "Music Box Dancer". I currently have it on what sounds like a mariachi band playing "March of the Toreadors" from Carmen which is kind of hilarious but I can't imagine what maniac would want to be alerted by that in their house ever. Most of the rest of the songs are like that.
text_fidelity_b: 1/2Mile Solar Driveway Alarm System-Up to 70FT Wide Sensor Range 3 Adjustable Sensitivities-Fully Weatherproof Outdoor Motion Sensor&Detector DIY Security Alert System

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire E 15 E5-575-33BM 15.6-Inch Full HD Notebook (Intel Core i3-7100U Processor 7th Generation , 4GB DDR4, 1TB 5400RPM Hard Drive, Intel HD Graphics 620, Windows 10 Home), Obsidian Black I did a little homework and this machine, especially at the price looked excellent. I noticed in reading Amazon reviews that a small percentage of buyers had received machines with faulty screens. So I went to BestBuy to see what they had, and found nothing appealing in any where near this price. So I ordered one. It arrived on Wednesday (days matter in this little story). Knowing there was a slight risk, I opened everything very carefully, saved everything in case I'd want to return it. Sure enough I got one with a faulty screen. However I'd also calculated the odds: very slim chance of getting two in a row. Thursday we started what I thought was likely to be a tricky, time consuming effort: filling forms, emails, getting to UPS, etc etc. It went like this: one click to get to the trade request on the Amazon order, five minutes to complete it ....Including a stunning question: did I want to drop the first one at UPS, or have them pick it up at my door? UPS would have the prepaid return label with them.
Then they shipped the replacement to me Thursday. SAME DAY! Monday the new one arrived, the man had the return label in his hand.He took one look at my shipping ready packaged box, slapped the label on, and left while I watched still in disbelief. This is way beyond 5 stars for Amazon.

And true to the odds, this machine I'm using for this is flawless. I love it. It's everything it is advertised to be, and more. The slowness some mentioned was easily remedied for my use by clearing the "Start Up", using Blackle as a homepage, and one click to change the "Next Window" screen. I don't play complex games, just puzzles, solitaire and the like so no need for speed there. Pictures, movies and TV are all beautiful, and quick to load.

The Windows 10 Home is surprisingly user friendly...and I'm 72. The machine runs cool, easy to upgrade, and most of all: affordable. So don't be afraid to take a chance if you're waffling. Thank you Amazon! Very much.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire E 15 E5-575-33BM 15.6-Inch Full HD Notebook (Intel Core i3-7100U Processor 7th Generation , 4GB DDR4, 1TB 5400RPM Hard Drive, Intel HD Graphics 620, Windows 10 Home), Obsidian Black

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150)) UPDATE: Six months in, this router has been flawless. AND I've discovered it has its own dynamic DNS support capability. That's a nice feature if you run any sort of server application. So, I continue to be impressed with this product.

---

I will be keeping a close eye on this router, which I just purchased yesterday, because it seems too good to be true. So far, in my 24 hours of usage since purchasing it for $29 at Walmart (sorry, Amazon, I was in a hurry) I have found it to be flexible and powerful in my unusual application, which is remote and requires 100% uptime with occasional bursts of heavy usage. Mine is a factory-fresh rather than refurb unit, incidentally.

I'll admit I had some trouble believing a router this cheap could be as good as this one turned out to be (assuming it stays reliable-- but, the one I bought trumpets a lifetime guarantee on the box). I expected something dumbed-down, with seriously constrained functionality and annoying firmware. (This model's v3 hardware, although Broadcom BCM5356-based, is not compatible with alternative firmware such as DD-WRT due to its problematic NVRAM size.) It's a single-stream design, with an internalized antenna, potentially suggesting performance limitations. And it's from Netgear, which I've frankly not had great luck with before... but it's been years since I've tried one of their products, and the reviews here are generally good. Most of the negative reviews here relate to support experiences, but my networking knowledge-level is expert, so ...what the heck, did I mention it was $29? An easy roll of the dice.

Though my application requires custom configuration, I initially started the unit using its web-based wizard, which you access by connecting your computer (via cable or WiFi) and pointing your browser to 192.168.1.1. With the unit connected to my cable modem, it set itself up quickly and voila, Internet. For most people this would be good enough and the job would be done. Kudos to Netgear for delivering the product with WPA-2 encryption enabled! They provide a SSID and password on a printed label. So, you're good to go. And its default configuration is just fine for most folks' usage.

For my application, however, I needed to cable several devices including a VoIP adaptor (a la [...] and a server with several ports exposed to the Internet. The unit needed to be set to a specific IP address scheme, SSID and password. And a dynamic-DNS utility on the server needed to communicate with my DNS provider. ...To accomplish these and other advanced tasks, the browser-based configurator at 192.168.1.1 has an Advanced tab. Proceeding through the settings is straightforward and similar to other reasonably-configurable routers. The default settings established earlier by the wizard remain intact in the Advanced panes so you are starting from a known-operable configuration. All good.

So I proceeded through each of my customizations, taking care to click the Apply button after modifying any pane. Usually there's a ten-second delay during which the unit sets up the new settings; a few necessitate that the router reboot itself. Everything went smoothly.

So, for $29 I'd replicated an unusual configuration and everything was working. But how well?

Okay so my wife had to take an important international FaceTime call as I was finishing up. So, for a while there the server was downloading some massive updates, two ssh clients were talking to the server, VoIP was in use, six WiFi clients were doing whatever they were doing, a 3G microcell tower was initializing and downloading firmware updates to itself ...and FaceTime was running smoothly with a high frame-rate on her third-gen iPad. A nice acid test!

In particular, I did not feel the need to mess with the unit's default QoS settings... and additional props to Netgear for including QoS in a router this inexpensive!

So far, I'm impressed. It's hard to imagine a better value in a router. I'll update this review if there are any reliability issues, but so far, so good. So excellent, in fact.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150))

text_fidelity_a:
Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black Reviewed by my husband, a photography enthusiast.

Over the last 20 years, my husband has purchased several LowePro camera bags/backpacks (i.e., Mini Trekker & Micro-Trekker 100). He has found that they have been some of the best he has ever owned. He prefers backpacks because they are easy to carry and keep up with, especially if you are on the go. Backpacks also allow for easy storage and are super convenient. They give you freedom of movement and your hands are free to capture those special moments that you may not otherwise get if you were holding a bag in your hand. The Viewpoint (LowePro) BP 250 is the perfect addition to his bag collection especially since it is specially designed for small video equipment.

Here’s what he liked:

• This bag is attractive. The design is smart, functional and full of surprises. The Viewpoint BP250 is well-made with plenty of room for your Go Pro and accompanying equipment. There is a ton of storage (inside and out). There are several compartments where you can store your accessories, cords, lenses and other equipment. On the outside of the main bag, there is a zipper pocket (which allows for small items like a memory stick/card or thumbdrive). There is a pocket on the other side of the bag which will fit a small tripod or other item (like an umbrella). The entire bag can be zippered so you won’t lose any of your accessories.

• It is ideal for those who use (small) video and other digital equipment. There is a space dedicated to a small computer. While this backpack will not allow you to carry one of the larger sized laptops (our 17” didn’t fit), it has adequate space for the smaller ones (about 15”), a SurfacePro, iPad or other small notebook or tablet. He finds that the option of carrying a computer is great because it will allow you to quickly upload and edit your videos wherever you are. There is no reason to wait….just review, edit (if needed), and upload!

• The straps are unlike the traditional ones that come straight down the shoulders. The BP250 LowePro’s straps are curved which he found to be less stress on his shoulders. After some adjustments (he’s 6’1, average sized with average shoulders), it was a good fit. The straps are slightly padded and comfortable. There are small snaps that lock the straps in place to ensure that they don’t fall down when walking or hiking.

• There is a small (lunch box sized bag) that can be removed and can hold your GoPro camera and equipment. Once closed, it fits directly into your main LowePro Bag. It is padded and once inside, will protect your camera and smaller lenses. Or if you want, this smaller bag can be used instead of taking the large one.

• This bag comes with a rain cover. Not sure how much you will use this feature, but if you are ever caught in a drizzle or rain storm, there is a plastic cover that can be removed (unzipped) from the bottom and cover your bag. This is perfect for keeping your bag and equipment dry.

• The price. While this bag may seem a little pricey (about $130) it’s worth it. The craftsmanship and functionality will prove invaluable for the amateur or professional photographer. It’s a small investment with some heavy returns. You’ve got protection and functionality.

Overall, my husband gives this bag 5 stars. He finds that it is not only good to use for a GoPro, but other small video and photography equipment. Backpacks are useful for photographers because they allow your hands to be free to capture those moments or events as they unfold. In the past he has purchased Lowepro equipment and found them to be sturdy and durable, and the Viewpoint BP250 is not different. It looks good and he won’t leave home without it.
text_fidelity_b: Lowepro LP36915 ViewPoint CS 40 - A Soft-Sided Protective Case for a Smartphone, GoPro or 360 Camera and Accessories,Black

text_fidelity_a:
SENTRY V1.0 Dual Mode Call Blocker I've been relying on a cordless phone system with built-in call blocking, but it only stores 30 numbers. That gets filled up in short order, and I delete them and start over. I needed something better.

And this is definitely better. I'm using it with a cable-provided phone line and cordless phone system. And it works. Mostly.

The cool thing about this system is it intercepts everything by default, and announces that if the caller is a telemarketer, to remove us from their call list. It also announces that the caller can press "0" for the call to go through. This eliminates all robocalls, and most other unsolicited calls.

After the phone number is in the device's caller ID memory, you can then whitelist or blacklist it if you choose. Whitelisted numbers go straight through without an announcement and ring the phone normally. Blacklisted numbers are simply blocked. You might hear a partial ring, but that's the end of it.

There are a couple of down sides. When a caller presses "0", only the ringer in the device itself rings. It does not ring the phone system. If you're not near the room where the device is, chances are you won't hear it. So if you're expecting important calls, it's probably best to set the device to "off" when you're not within earshot of it.

And the other is -- and this may be a fault in the particular unit I received -- the "off" position is not always reliable. More than once it has continued to block calls when set to "off." If a really important call is expected, I'll probably just disconnect the unit from the phone system completely.

Other than that, it's effective. It blocks unwanted calls.
text_fidelity_b: SENTRY V1.0 Dual Mode Call Blocker

ASUS Transformer Infinity TF700T Mobile Docking - Champagne I bought this at the same time I bought an Infinity TF700. I'm glad I did. I find screen touchpad typing difficult and I have pretty big hands. The keys on this are quite nice. Very good positive feel and comparable to most laptop keyboards. Complete set of Android function keys that cover just about everything. No need to be touching the screen. I wish the mouse pad was just a bit better. It's more than functional I guess. It's not bad, but it isn't great either. But I'm not a big fan of mouse pads anyway so I might be a bit over critical in this regard. .

The unit connects and disconnects nicely and has a lock lever which latches automatically. You can open it to about a 140 degree angle which makes getting a comforatble viewing angle possible in virtually any situation. If feels quite solid with no free play. Nice snug fit.

It gives you another battery too that adds 4.5 hours of uptime. You also get a standard sized USB 2.0 port and SD card reader. The USB port can operate in "host mode" allowing you to connect a variety of devices that should couple automatically. Can't say that I've used the USB a lot yet.

It is a very nice addition to a great tablet that gives you a laptop PC feel. It is tapered a little in thickness being a bit thicker at the back, but overall not much thicker than the tablet itself. Folded closed with the TF700 attached it's about 3/4 inch thick at the most and makes a nice sleek package. Connected together the two weigh right at 2.5 lbs.

The current price seems a bit high compared to other tablet's docking ports, but the keyboard is superior and the other features are quite nice. It's a worthwhile addition. I'd give it 5 stars if it were about $50 cheaper.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS Transformer Infinity TF700T Mobile Docking - Champagne

text_fidelity_a:
Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation) The Flip is a pint-sized camcorder with a surprising feature set given its compactness. Though is it not a full-featured camcorder and I would not recommend it for serious recording (special events or production material), it is excellent for on-the-go shots and for spontaneous recording when opportunities present themselves.

The Flip is small - a little smaller than an ice cream sandwich. It may be little, but there's tremendous convenience in being able to drop your camcorder in your shirt pocket or your purse and have it at the ready. This compact size holds everything you need to start recording - batteries, flash RAM and all. Without tapes or DVD media on which to record, there's little reason for this device to be any bigger.

It is a solid little thing and feels durable. That doesn't mean it would do well if dropped or stepped on, but it likely will be ok if jostled a little.

Recording is simple. No, I should be more clear - recording with the Flip is trivial. There is no real science to using it: turn it on, point and press record. Press the record button again to stop recording. Even technological novices, or people afraid of electronics will have no trouble using the Flip to record. Playing back is equally simple - once the recording is finished, press the Play button.

There are + and - buttons, used for Zoom. The Flip doesn't have a particularly capable zoom, so shooting from a distance will not yield especially great results.

I tested this camcorder in my basement on a bright, sunny day, and I wandered about recording and chattering to myself. When I played back what I had recorded, I made a pleasant discovery - it does some light balancing and deals with changes in light levels so that the video is still clear. The sound is also good, better than I expected. When I walked down a dark hallway and into an unlit room, it had tried very hard to accommodate for the lack of light but it was unable to completely overcome the darkness. As there is no light on the camcorder to come on when it is dark, this is understandable, but it did surprisingly well in spite of that.

I attached the Flip to my computer to pull the video to my hard drive. FlipShare installed itself and started up, seeing the video I had made. It allowed me to pull it over and even gave me the option to delete it from the camera. Once finished, I was able to play the video through FlipShare. Instead, I decided to hunt it down and use a different application to play it.

I found the file and tried to open it with Windows Media Player. I got audio, but not video. When I switched to QuickTime, my video came up and filled my screen. This is the point at which I made an unfortunate discovery. Every minute move I had made while recording was now plainly obvious, as there is no anti-jitter built into the device.

The video, on a 1440x900 resolution screen, looked clear. It records at 1280x720, which is not that much smaller, so I was a little surprised. I would have expected a little pixelation, but this actually was not an issue.

There are few settings that can be adjusted on the Flip - language, date, time and recording light.

The Flip is a nice camcorder that provides tremendous convenience and fun. It is very easy to use and very compact. It is important to remember that it has some limitations which make it a less-than-ideal choice for more serious application, but if those limitations are not an issue for you then the Flip is a fun and affordable way to capture things on video.
text_fidelity_b: Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black) An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.
text_fidelity_b: Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer" My household has a variety of headphone fans in it. The headphone level of appreciation varies from "I will listen to anything as long as it works" to "I don't hear that sound exactly as I want to, so these are no good". I am in the middle. I love a good headphone, but I am not addicted to analyze every single sound and micro focus on them. What I am looking for is a headphone which has good sound separation, realistic presentation, but not too much distortion or muffled sound.

My purpose for wanting headphones with a cord was duo-fold. I want a set of headphones to listen to my desktop or laptop in my living room while people are watching TV, and I also wanted a set of headphones for my tablet so I could watch video demonstrations for my spinning wheel, knitting, and other crafts in the living room while the rest of the family is watching TV and I need to a quick refresher on a project I am working on.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
In the box (a nice box with excellent protection for the headphones), there is a set of headphones, two cords, and an extra plug adapter. The headphones themselves are lightweight for what they are. They are marked R and L so that you will put them on the correctly way easily. The ear cushions are a velveteen fabric which a lightweight foam inside. The cord jack is on the left ear phone. The top of the headphones has a soft leatherette foam which is very soft and easily squished.

The long cord measures about 118 inches. It comes with a large jack for stereos on one end and the smaller jack which fits into the headphones. The additional adapter for the smaller jack which fits into phones and tablets. The smaller cord measures approximately 48 inches and has a phone answering. This one has a smaller jack for phones and tablets.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES FIT?
I found that these headphones fit everyone in the family very nicely. Even my headphone fanatic liked them although he said his phones were a little nicer but not much.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I really like these. I have tried them with music, videos, movies, and other sounds from classes to classical. I find them to be realistic and high quality. It feels like I am in the room with the sounds - hearing squeaking of chairs, or fingers on strings - but yet it feels more natural than sound proof headphones. I can still hear what is going on around me, so if really loud music is happening in the room, these are not overly helpful, but that does not happen here so I am fine with them.

I found the sound clarity to be nice. No muffled sounds or blurry sound with these that I have noticed thus far. The bass is nice- not too much, but not overwhelming either. Of course, that depends on the recording I am listening to. There are no controls on the headphones.

Due to the cushioning these are comfortable. If I have a tender head (such as headache type day) they tend to hit a sensitive area of my head so I can not wear them as long as I would like, but most of the time, I can wear them comfortably for extended periods of time. It is nice because I can hear what is going on in the room around me if I need to so it does not block me from having to pay attention to things around me when necessary.

HOW DO THESE WORK WITH A TABLET?
I found these to work very well with my tablet. Using them for visual lessons at my spinning wheel and knitting chair is perfect- just what I wanted. I can hear what I need and not feel closed in with them on either.

CAN OTHER PEOPLE HEAR THEM IN A QUIET ROOM?
That is the one drawback about these headphones- if you are in a library, or quiet room, people around you will be able to hear what you are listening to unless it is very low volume and then you will have to strain to hear.

HOW DO THEY WORK WITH A PHONE?
I have not used them with my phone yet so have not had the chance to use the phone features. I tend to use my tablet most of the time. I will update when I have experience in that area to add.

OTHER COMMENTS
My son who is the headphone fanatic was even impressed with these headphones. He has several top line headphones (including Turtle Beach) and said that he was very impressed by the definition of sound, balanced bass and treble and clarity of these headphones. From him that is a compliment. He is rather stingy with glowing comments on most things electronic.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For the price of these headphones, this is a really nice set. Sound is clear, balanced, and realistic. The headphones are comfortable and well cushioned, making them wearable for extended periods of time. Lots of great sound and detail, yet the ability to hear the room around make them practical for use in a multitasking situation. They work great with tablets, laptops, and desktop although I have not tested a lot with my phone yet, my son has and they work great.

RATING
FIVE stars for these headphones. I am very happy with them. I plan to test in the future for gaming and phone answering and will update at that time.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer"

MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame I love technology, but I can't navigate new tech as easily as I used to. I fear that I'm turning into my parents, who needed my help with programming the VCR. These days, everything seems to have software that you must navigate, and it is seldom as intuitive as it once was for me.

This frame was easy to figure out, though, at least for the features I care about. I skipped right over the parts where it wanted to connect to my network and so forth. I just wanted to upload photos from a micro-SD card, and then have it play them back to me. And it does that very well.

It has a light sensor that adjusts the brightness of the screen automatically if you enable it to, which is a very nice feature that is lacking on my other digital picture frames. I was also able to program it to go to sleep when I'm never up, to save on energy. I didn't want it to be motion activated, as I want it to be displaying photos the moment I walk into the room. Fortunately, this feature is already off by default.

The frame looks really nice, with a small "mat" border around the display. This mat is something that most digital frames are lacking, and let me tell you, this tiny feature makes a huge difference. It really sells the idea that this is a picture frame, instead of merely a digital display. I can't say enough about how much this improves the aesthetic of this frame.

I have a couple of digital frames that I use in a horizontal orientation, so I deleted all my vertical photos from them and moved them onto this one instead, and set it up in a vertical orientation. It is so nice to have the frame matched to the orientation of the photos! You don't get those huge bars on the sides or top/bottom, or if you have it set to crop then you don't crop out 2/3 of the photo!

I have no complaints about this digital photo frame. I can't speak for all of the features, because I have no use for some of them. But the features I wanted work great, and the frame itself looks fantastic!
text_fidelity_b: MOOLINK WiFi Digital Photo Frame, 1920 * 1200 Full HD Display, 1080P Digital Picture Frame, 10.1 inch Touch Screen, 16GB Storage, Share Photos via App or Email, Smart WiFi Electronic Picture Frame

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black Do not buy this if you're looking for the fastest tablet. That's not what it is, though it's by no means slow. It will take a lot more abuse than the fastest tablets available for the same price. You can stand outside in the rain or snow and use the touchscreen when it's wet. You can drop it in the mud, pick it up, wipe it off, and keep using it. I wouldn't take it scuba diving though. I will take it off-roading. This one has enough storage to preload maps for off-road hiking/biking/riding/driving for when there's no signal at all.

I've seen several questions about whether this works with Verizon, and several people answer that it doesn't. Those people are wrong. The Enterprise/LTE/4G/WiFi version does work with Verizon. It should work with others. Find this model number (SM-T577UZKGN14) on the Samsung site to check. Samsung knows. Those other people don't.

This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two.

I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps.

So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon.

Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed.

Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU.

From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged.

Con: The biggest downside to these is that there's no external charger that I can find for the replaceable battery. At least I can't find one. Maybe one exists. I have no evidence of that. It is possible to buy another compatible battery, but I can't find any way to charge said battery other than to charge it in the tablet, and it's a pain to get to, because of the lengths Samsung went to to seal the battery compartment. The battery life is substantial, partly due to the less-than-premium performance, but it would really be nice to be able to easily carry a fully-charged spare.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active3 Enterprise Edition 8” Rugged Multi Purpose Tablet |128GB & WiFi | Biometric Security (SM-T570NZKEN20), Black

IFOOTAGE On-Camera Video Light, RGB Led light for Photography, APP Control/Keyframes, CRI 95+/2700-10000K, 2000mAh/Type C Charging, Mobile Video Cconference Light, Multiple Mounting Methods, C4/Yellow I'm impressed. This little guy is strong and bright! I've tried several lights, including handheld (like this), panel lights, ring lights, etc., and I have been very impressed with this one.

Before I dive into the good, let me discuss the bad: the iPhone app. I'm all for having an app to control the light and I totally understand why it's necessary. HOWEVER, this app REQUIRES that you sign up with an email and password. While there might be benefits to this (like accessing presets/settings across devices); I didn't check. Registering an account should 100% be optional. There is no reason to require me to register with my email + password so I can control this light via Bluetooth. As an aside, according to the Apple App Store, the developer does not collect any data from your phone (see pic); this is the reason I did not deduct a star for this.

My second gripe with the app, is that the it is a little rudimentary. Not particularly polished; and a little buggy at times (e.g. I couldn't get effects to kick in after selecting them on the app (I'd have to do it multiple times before the light would react), the light wouldn't always connect on the first try, etc. This was not the norm, but it happened a few times during my testing.

Now onto the good: First and foremost, it is BRIGHT. Brighter than similarly-sized lights. Physically, it feels well-designed. It has a 2000 mAh battery (I expected 1000 mAh). It is intuitive to operate and you can use it without the app if necessary (setting color temp, intensity, etc. No effects). There is a USB-C port for charging and a small display on the top, which shows battery %, time remaining (!), and color settings.

Overall, I have been really pleased with this light.

Fellowes I-Spire Series Laptop Lift/Stand, White/Gray (9311201) Before this stand, I used another Fellowes one for my laptop at home, and it proved its worth--for a while. However, with my new desk setup, I needed something which I could use while changing the height and angle of my laptop screen in a way the old stand simply couldn't. I have a Unicomp keyboard and Logitech mouse which I prefer using, and my "home" laptop needed a better stand.
Enter this Lift.

I've seen many angled laptop stands, and that's what I had in mind when I wanted to switch my old one out. Plus, my old one was better suited for the monitor at work, so I wanted to take that when I had the chance. Finally, I had the opportunity to get an angled one, so I jumped on it.

I'm not using this stand with my laptop by itself. I'm using it as a supplemental to "lift" it up with my home desktop setup being my keyboard and mouse. For that, the stand works marvelously. The angle and height are just about right; I no longer have to arch my neck uncomfortably forward. Plus, I can take my old stand to work and finally have proper posture there too.
I can't see using this by itself. My hands would quickly become painfully uncomfortable. Heck, I can't stand using keyboards with their built-in mini stands. I honestly don't know why they're there; the angle cramps my wrists very fast.

So for my use, I think the stand is great. There's even some empty real estate near the back to put things under, and it seems sturdy enough overall. It's currently holding my Toshiba 17" Windows PC, which is snugly fit.
text_fidelity_b: Fellowes I-Spire Series Laptop Lift/Stand, White/Gray (9311201)

Option 1 was to buy this fan and create a recess in the lid of my case to mount it (the reason I chose this slim fan over a more powerful 25mm thick fan). Option 2 was to shell out three or four times what this fan costs for a slim CPU cooler (my case is quite small) and hope that it works better than the stock Intel cooler.

I went with the more budget friendly Option 1, took the time to create the 15mm recess, and am happy to report that my idle temp dropped 15* (33* C vs 48) and after half an hour of CPU torture with Prime95, it was holding steady at 60* C (still 12* shy of the max temp for this CPU). I have the fan mounted horizontally (not ideal for a sleeve bearing fan like this, I know) and while I understand that my use case isn't typical, I'm quite happy with my purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I have had the opportunity to review a few similar products over the last couple years and this new security light by Sentry has some great features that make it a stand out among other security lights.

I found installation straightforward and simple. For those who have trouble connecting to your WiFi, the most common issue is the strength of the different frequencies your router is broadcasting. The easiest way to resolve this is to go into your router settings via your computer and turn off the 5 GHz band during setup. This is necessary sometimes when initially setting up SmartHome products. While some may find this necessary for this product, I did not using my Orbi router system.

The Geeni App is easy to use and makes setup and customization of how the light operates user friendly.

This unit puts out a huge amount of light - 2100 Lumens to be exact while only using 24 watts of power thanks to it utilizing the LED bulbs.

This is the first security bulb I have reviewed that actually has a built in siren. This could be an outstanding feature if needed. Whether utilized to scare off someone attempting to break in to your home or to cause unwanted pests to run the other way - it will work! This siren is effective because it’s loud.

The speaker can also be used for communication purposes. By utilizing a built in microphone you’ll be able to have conversations with those you are viewing through the camera. The speaker and microphone have a surprisingly high clarity. The only thing I found odd with this aspect of this product is this is not a light you’ll want to place at head height as the light is so bright and the camera is really made to provide a wide angle view. Therefore when you speak through the speaker I found people usually look around and can’t figure out the source of the disembodied voice.

After using this product for the last 6 weeks I have found that it performs excellently. By installing a 128GB micro SD card within it, saving videos is easy and I’ve had plenty of time to review the footage. I love that it holds the recording locally so there is no cloud subscription fee required.

This is an excellent security light that will not only light the night when motion is detected, but will record it, alert you, scare the intruder with a siren or allow you to speak to them (or apologize for just scaring them with the siren).

This is an outstanding product that I definitely recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google

Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector I was actually really shocked at how great this little portable speaker is. My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. In fact, the bass was so effective out of this thing that some of my favorite songs made it dance around the table.

I love that it is so much louder than the music I get out of my cell phone, and I also love that I can listen to hip-hop and rap and enjoy actual bass, which usually doesn't come through for my cell phone speaker at all.

You can actually control the music from your cell phone from the speaker itself. It has a pause/play button, forward and back, and volume controls. It also has a speakerphone control, in case you wanted to have a quick conversation from the speaker itself. I would not personally want to use the speaker as a speakerphone, but it is nice to have the option in a pinch.

The one thing I didn't care for is that when you tap the volume button and it hits its maximum, it beeps at you to let you know that it won't go any louder. It's a pretty annoying sound, and in my view they could just have left that feature out. I'm sure I would figure it out soon enough that it wouldn't go any louder.

Overall, I was really surprised at the quality, ease of setup, and range of sound from this cute little speaker. I'm delighted to own it, and anticipate it getting a lot of use over the coming months and years.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector
