Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H Though I received this Acer Chromebook for review, I have another one exactly like it that I bought refurbished about a month ago and have been using it a lot. They are both the same make and model. What I like:

1. The battery life is exceptionally long. I can get a long play list going and it will run all night with nearly a full battery in the morning. I'm using Bluetooth earbuds and I darken the screen so I'm sure that helps to save on battery power.
2. Connects quickly with all my Bluetooth earbuds (and I have several). Only one set of earbuds won't connect and I am still trying to figure that out.
3. Boots up quickly - very short wait time.
4. Screen is nice and big and easy to see.
5. Touchpad works great.
6. Keyboard feels good to use and I'm a very fast typer.
7. It was easy to get it started and on-line right out of the box. It didn't ask me for a billion passwords.

What could be better:
1. Sound is rather weak and really not very good.
2. Screen quality (color, brightness, clarity, etc....) is average
3. Seems to be kind of slow going from site to site....my desktops are much faster.
4. It seems this Acer chromebook doesn't send a Bluetooth signal (weaker) as far as my old Haier chromebook. If I want to listen to something while in bed I have to move the Acer to the bottom of the stairs so the signal will reach. Never had that problem before.

But, for the price of this chrombook (as of this review it's around $179.00) I think it's an excellent buy. It comes with a power cord (of course) but that's it. It uses the Chrome web browser and all I want it for is to check a few sites, write reviews and cruise Youtube. It would be great for college/high school students and anyone who doesn't mind storing their data in the cloud. My main reason for using Chromebooks is that you don't have to buy anti-virus for them since they can't download any data so working off line is not feasible.

It seems to be constructed well and I'm happy with the refurb, but now hubs can use one to surf the web too.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Atom X5-E8000 Quad-Core Processor, 15.6" HD, 4GB LPDDR3, 16GB eMMC, CB3-532-108H

text_fidelity_a:
Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout First let me tell you what I like about this keyboard: I like the key action. Keys have a decently long stroke and are easy to press and don't feel spongy. I like the split layout, which makes for a much more natural position for the arms. I like the split spacebar. To me, these are advantages over the Logitech K350 I've been using, which has a curved, not split, key layout and a spongy feel when typing.

What I don't like, and what was pretty much a dealbreaker to me (I thought about returning it almost immediately) is the "wrist rest." It is short and rolls off steeply and provides no wrist support at all, unless you like typing with your wrist positioned lower than your knuckles and your hands bent upwards from the wrist. The recommended position is wrist level with the knuckles, which is called the "neutral" position. I personally prefer typing with my wrists positioned slightly higher than my knuckles.

Look at the product photos and notice that the typist doesn't even have his wrist on the wrist rest. He or she is using a hover hand technique, I guess to make things look more ergonomic or something, because if their wrists were actually on the wrist rest, their hands would be obviously bent upwards at the wrists to reach the keys.

I'm at a loss as to why many keyboard manufacturers (including Logitech with the K350) provide legs to raise the back of the keyboard and don't provide anything to raise the front. That just makes the "backwards" bend at the wrist even more pronounced.

This Periboard keyboard is no exception to that. It has foldaway legs at the back and none in the front. But even if it had legs to raise the front, it wouldn't provide much improvement. I raised the front a couple of inches with a foam wedge I use for keyboard support, and the wrist rest was still so low I pressed the spacebar when reaching for the F2 key.

I even tried adding foam wrist rests but the built-in rest is so steep and short it actually interferes with using a really functional rest. I even tried using wearable wrist rests---which are kind of annoying on their own since they aren't all that stable---and the steep slope and short length of the built-in wrist rest made that a less than effective solution. This keyboard might have been a lot better if it had no built-in wrist rest at all. That way you could use your own and set it up just like you like it.

It's disappointing, actually. I like the key action and layout, but the wrist rest pretty much nerfs the whole thing. I may keep it and experiment with solutions from time to time. I might even see if I can cut off the built-in rest and replace it with something made of wood or something, or just get it out of the way so I can use some other effective wrist rest.

In the meantime, I'm probably going to stick with the spongy-action, non-split Logitech K350. In fact I'm typing this review on it, though I would have liked to use the Periboard 512. But until I come up with a better wrist rest solution it's just easier to use the K350.

And a couple more quick points, comparing this keyboard to the K350, this keyboard is wired while the K350 is wireless. The overall footprint of both (length and width) is almost the same. I personally don't use or need the multimedia keys on either.

Because of the better key action and, to me, better key layout, if it had a better wrist rest, or none at all, this Periboard 512 might have become my go-to keyboard.
text_fidelity_b: Perixx Periboard-512 Ergonomic Split Keyboard - Natural Ergonomic Design - Black - Bulky Size 19.09"x9.29"x1.73", US English Layout

Ballistix Sport SODIMM 16GB Kit 8GBx2 DDR3 1600 MT/s PC3-12800 CL9 at 1.35V 204-Pin Memory BLS2C8G3N169ES4 This review is for the Crucial Ballistix Sports XT 16 Gig DIMM kit.

I was a little concerned with the DIMMs as they were a little fatter than normal, but they snapped easily into my Dell desktop computer. Both Windows 7 and Ubuntu recognized the memory at once, with no issues, which really was to be expected.

Often, I'll run multiple VMs at a time. I do software development, so often I'll have one VM running Windows Server 2008, hosting SQL Server, while a second acts as a development box, and a third, which is frequently wiped out and recreated (or really, cloned from a blank copy) acts as a testing machine. Each of these machines gets 4 gig dedicated ram, and I leave the last 4 for the host OS. This RAM has held up to that kind of intense use without any problem. I am delighted.

text_fidelity_a:
PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor I have been wanting to get a bluetooth speaker for connecting to my tablet for a while so I was very pleased to get an opportunity to try this speaker set. It is far and away better than what I originally had in mind and so far I am more than pleased with them.

Setup of these speakers is straightforward and simple, so much so that instructions really are not needed to get started. The wire connector is color-coded to make connecting the speakers to each other almost completely foolproof. If I have any complaints about the setup it would be that the wire connector is a little on the short side but that’s an easy fix - just buy longer wire.

I enabled bluetooth on my tablet, told the speaker set to make itself available and the tablet connected to it immediately. One could not ask for anything simpler. The process took less than a minute and most of that time was spent walking across the room to press the bluetooth button on the speakers.

I loaded up Pandora and told the tablet to play and almost immediately it was clear that these speakers are far above average. The sound profile is stunning - clear and crisp highs, rich midrange and very satisfying bass without overdriving. These speakers do an outstanding job of accurately reproducing the sound. On the back of the main (control) speaker there are two knobs for adjusting the highs and lows should the middle be unsatisfactory for some reason. These speakers also do a good job with spacial elements and there is depth to the sound.

I paired the speakers with my laptop (once I powered off the tablet) as well and it was also very easy.

I took some cables and wired the speakers to an older television in the house to see how much better watching TV would be. It was definitely better and it have a more spacial and stereo sound experience but with our TV this prevented us from making any volume adjustments unless we turned the volume knob on the speaker itself. This is a minor nuisance but certainly not a real issue.

In addition to great sound, these seem to be well-build and rugged, a good sign right out of the box. These are an excellent choice for a home theater system or an audiophile's listening room.

So far I have found nothing about which to complain with these speakers. Set-up is a snap and the sound quality is just amazing. These are speakers for the serious listener.
text_fidelity_b: PreSonus C3.5 BT Channel Studio Monitor

- go on runs while listening to music
- ignore noisy people around me
- get myself into a state of focus

- show people I am not interested to talk to them
- as a fashion statement

Seriously, I wear these so much I think I am developing a bald spot. Maybe that's why all the engineers are bald. The sound quality is superb, and so is the bluetooth range and connectivity. I have since tried the Sony's, Dolby dimensions, the newer model of these, but these are the best one. I have bought a pair for my whole family, and replaced my old pair when it got old without a second thought. One time, I tried my friend's airpods and almost threw up at the sound quality. text_fidelity_a:
Apple 12.9-inch iPad Pro Wi-Fi + Cellular - 12.9" Tablet - 256 GB - 3G/4G - GOLD There is so much talk about the declining sales of iPad. So much so, the discussion might influence a potential buyer to pause before buying or not buy at all, and instead buy a competing tablet or laptop. I think the key to making a decision to buy the iPad Pro lies in a wallpaper Apple provided with the very first version of iPad. It was a licensed photograph of Pyramid Lake by Robert Misrach. The exposure, made at night, appears to be in daylight. The clue that it was a night time photograph are the star trails that resulted from the long exposure. The lake surface appears as smooth as a mirror. The mirror surface of the lake in this photograph enables the viewer to immerse himself or herself in the device, making it a perfect fulfillment of whatever there desires might be "for iPad". The iPad is a perfect "evocative object", evoking whatever feelings and intentions the iPad user brings to it. That is why the iPad is so undefinable and uncategorizable. It is is whatever ever we want it to be.....and with iPad Pro Apple reaches again for that elusive quality.

After 7 days with the new Apple iPad Pro I am happy that I followed my hunch that the iPad Pro would be better for me than a laptop for a mobile multi-purpose device. I am very pleased how the slide over multitasking works. Bigger is better whether using multi-tasking features live slide over and picture-in-picture. The user does not get poorly sized Windows for both applications. For example if your browser is open in one window, and photos is open in a second, but applications are scaled to size in each window.

I purchased the 32MB version because I tend to use iCloud to store photos, music, documents. I only need local storage for IOS apps and the few documents I need.

I purchased a black rear cover, and a contrasting white front cover. The only accessory I use so far is the Apple Pencil for drawing in Paper by 53 and Apple Notes ( to take notes in my University classes ). I use the iPad Pro almost exclusively landscape or horizontal, the only iPad that can be used in portrait is the Mini. At the time I purchased the iPad Pro the wait times for shipment of the Apple Pencil was 4-5 weeks. However, I was able to find one locally at my University Bookstore. I am concentrating on using the Apple Pencil at the moment, using just the on-screen keyboard. I have an open mind about buying the iPad Pro keyboard in the future. However, the iPad is all about creating art through use of touch and the pencil right now. I don't want it to be a laptop. I want it to be a "blank sheet of paper".

The audio produced by the 4 speakers produce a very pleasing music listening experience without headphones.

One final note: it appears the iPad Pro includes technology that can be used in the future today's blog post in Daring Fireball notes that the Lightning connector includes support for USB 3.0, a much faster transfer speeds. It will be interesting to see what applications take advantage of that speed next year.
text_fidelity_b: Apple 12.9-inch iPad Pro Wi-Fi + Cellular - 12.9" Tablet - 256 GB - 3G/4G - GOLD

Included on the cable is a velcro strap that makes keeping things tidy either way.

I think this is a very useful cable - especially the addition of the LED will make it a companion in my travels. I recommend it.

Nexuslink Wave 2 G.hn Powerline Adapter | Pass-Through Outlet | 2000 Mbps I 2-Unit Kit I (GPL-2000PT-KIT) In terms of convenience, this is an outstanding product. It literally is plug and play. Just plug the transmitter in near you router and plug the Ethernet cable into an open port. Plug the receiver where you need the signal press the button on each device and setup is about complete. I had zero issues in terms of connection.

The farther the distance you span and the more walls and obstacles between, the slower the resultant signal will be. I tested the unit in a multitude of locations and I always received a signal, although it dropped the farther away I moved.

The point of this device is to use in locations where it is not possible, or where it would be difficult to run an Ethernet cable. If you are in a position where you need to get a signal to a TV to stream programming this would be a great choice. I tested it with Hulu, Prime and Netflix and it worked great. Depending on distance spanned and the strength of your original signal it probably would be adequate for internet use. However I can not recommend this as a viable option for gaming.

This set will definitely fulfill many people’s needs. It is just important to consider your use in relation to the WiFi product you install. For my family this worked fairly well.
text_fidelity_b: Nexuslink Wave 2 G.hn Powerline Adapter | Pass-Through Outlet | 2000 Mbps I 2-Unit Kit I (GPL-2000PT-KIT)

That card had followed me from a Note II to a Note 3 to my current Note 4. I was a little concerned about compatibility and reliability because a few years ago tried to save a buck by getting a tier 2 brand card that literally melted down.

This time I took a chance with this non-Samsung card and cannot be more pleased. For one thing, the transfer from my old card to this one did not cause this to get hot. Considering that there was about 29GB involved that was my first indication that this is a well made card.

Another thing is after I transferred the contents to this card (via a card reader), as soon as I popped it into my Note 4, it immediately mounted and everything on the older card was there. I took the time to look for corrupted files, sampled a lot of random music, and checked a few videos. Zero issues and the Note 4 did not balk at this card or any of the files on it.

As for speed, I am not going to make claims one way or the other. I did not test it with benchmarking software, and since I use this mainly for streaming music the additional speed (if any) is not noticeable anyway. What is noticeable is the total compatibility with my Note 4 and the extra breathing room the capacity provides me.

Overall I am not only pleased, I feel as though this card is a better value than the Samsung brand cards that I had been purchasing. And every bit as reliable too.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display I have unusual needs for the Kindle Touch. It is my study device. As an autodidact moving along in years I found that lugging a lot of textbooks/reference books/dictionaries around was getting in the way of learning. Sure, I can use a laptop for lots of online material to study but when I'm comfortable in my easy chair and the laptop is in the other room I just don't want to get up. Enter the Touch. I am reading philosophy and studying Latin on my own. I have loaded the Touch up with many free or low cost books on Aristotle and St. Thomas Aquinas. I have many personal Latin documents, some Latin readers and texts, Interlinear translation of the Douay-Rheims Bible, etc. Now I discover that I can save web pages in html file format and convert them to mobi format for the Touch and end up with "live" links to hundreds of web pages I am interested in using in my studies. I have sent these documents to the Touch either using the email forwarding capability or the conversion program directly(Calibre-free download. A terrific program recommended by a Kindle Touch tech services guy. Wouldn't be without it!) The Kindle Touch when hooked to my home wireless network downloads web pages very fast. I can look up anything I need on Latin grammar from the web and even bookmark pages I want to save for later use. If I'm out and about I can find any free Wi Fi location and log on and do the same.

The things that are invaluable and a couple are unique to the Touch--the Fire, or the iPad 3 cannot do them, are:

1. Change the default dictionary to Latin, or any language for which you can get a digital dictionary that works with Kindle Touch. I have two Latin dictionaries that cost nearly nothing! This is a great help to anyone trying to translate and learn a new language. If I can't find it in the default ditionary I am using I then work the magic of...............

2. Web search for Latin words. I can get Google Translate, the Whitaker Latin Dictionary, Perseus Latin Word Search, etc through the browser. Pages I want to use often I can Bookmark and open them through the Menu screen for the Touch. Then, and this is crucial...........

3. You can expand browser pages by a couple of taps or by the expanding finger touch move on the screen. Many Latin words are displayed in tables that are actually images and are really too small to deal with. Just hold your finger/stylus on the screen, the box pops up and the little magnifying glass with + sign in it appears. Press that and Voila! the image now fills the screen in comfortable text size. This can be done with books too and makes tables of conjugated verbs, noun declensions etc from texts and web pages super readable and thus useful.

4. Notes. Press an word that I want to look up later, type a note about my thought(s) or that I want to translate off the web later on, save it and then look up later in View Notes and Marks for the document/book I am working with. A great way to study!

5. The reading screen is so comfortable to use. Absolutely no glare and I cannot say that about Kindle Fire or iPads--anti-glare covers are a necessity with them. Just try to read something with the Fire on sunny day while sitting in the car waiting for your spouse to get finished shopping. Not easy. With the Touch it is simplicity in itself. Just turn on and read.

6. Many books have an interactive "live" table of contents. If I really want that in a book I download a sample first and check. If it doesn't have one I may not buy although you can navigate with page/location numbers if necessary. Just a bit more awkward.

7. Amount of stuff on the device. I have over 4000 pages of the works of St. Thomas Aquinas, Aristotle's complete works of his major writings, again nearly 1000 pages, several very large Latin textbooks, other philosophy books, three different copies of the Bible, etc etc. Probably approaching 7-8000 pages of material ALL AT MY FINGERTIPS!........Plus the web when near Wi Fi and connected.

My wife received her Touch from me for her birthday. She is a voracious reader of thriller/mystery novels, the Vince Flynn, David Baldacci, et. al., genre. Since she got the Kindle Touch her reading speed has increased noticeably. She can make the type as large as she wants it to be, adjust the interlinear gap and look up words she doesn't know with the default English dictionary that comes with the device.

Finally, I can charge my Touch, use it everyday, web time, download time, reading time and a lot of just looking at the screen "think time" I charge it about every two weeks. She does the same, maybe less frequently because she doesn't make the Internet demands on her device that I do on mine. The Fire or the iPad--admittedly devices with much more capability for complex displays, videos, etc can make 7-10 hours before a charge is required. That can be a problem for people on the move.

I am sure I will find other great uses for this device. So far, I can find no knocks at all. My wife had to exchange her first machine because the touch screen wasn't quite right. That was a snap. I have contacted Kindle Customer/Technical Service Support about 7-8 times with questions or wanting to return her first device(which was replaced with the new one by overnight shipment!!!!!!!!!!! At no charge. Had the new one before we had to send the old one back. That is customer service.) The people I have talked to are well-trained, smart, very easy to talk to and polite beyond my experience on the web. Amazon customer service is superior. That is a major selling point as well.

I do not work for Amazon, never heard of them until a few years ago and nobody has helped me learn to use my Touch or my wife's either beyond a few calls about things that were actually easy to take care of if I had only read the right page of the manual. I would buy Touch again in a second! At $99 for the one with ads, which I have, or my wife's without ads at $139 there is not better reading/study device available outside of a full-fledged laptop/desktop computer, and I hate to sit in front of them all day anyhow.

Thank you Amazon. You have scored 10+
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Touch, Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display

text_fidelity_a:
HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year) I was really looking forward to trying this tablet out. To date I'd had no exposure to Windows 8.1 or a dedicated Windows tablet. I have had a decent 10.1 inch Android tablet.

First are foremost, the elephant in the room... or rather, the mouse. This is a seven inch wide screen tablet. I have friends whose who online lives are conducted via five inch cell phone screens and they're happy with it. The screen on this tablet is nice. Don't get me wrong. I was able to stream from Amazon video in HD (720) and the video was crisp and clean. Images display well but, again, the screen is just seven inches. I can't imagine trying to be productive with something so small.

For a device with only one gig of RAM this runs Windows fairly well. I wws able to load several Windows programs including the Calibrě eBook manager which took a little longer to convert eBooks between formats but did the job. I also loaded a legacy email and Usenet program that I've been using for a decade or longer. Along with directly installed programs I also downloaded a handful of apps from the very buggy Microsoft app store. The store worked less than 50% of the time while I was trying this tablet out. I at one point had to resort to switching to a local login account and then back to my Hotmail logi. It only took about an hour of reading web forums to find that solution to the Windows app store refusing to work.

Two problems I ran into were the sound which is from a single speaker hidden in a slot on one of the short sides of the tablet. If you want to listen to anything other than the default Window's beeps and tones you'll want to pair this with a blue tooth speaker or headphones. The speaker in this tablet is deplorable. The next problem I had was the tablet runs HOT. I was running a program designed for Windows 98, downloading and reading posts un Usenet and viewing a few posted vacation and astronomy images and I had to stop. The tablet was so hot it was uncomfortable to hold and I worried it might overheat and become damaged.

While I was impressed to see Windows running on a small tablet I was thoroughly unimpressed with Windows 8.1 the tile system is just terrible.

So, it has good video quality on a too small screen with horrible sound and a flaky app store to rely upon, though you can download and install normal Windows programs. I just wasn't that crazy about this tablet. And will definitely be sticking with Android and a much larger screen.
text_fidelity_b: HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year)

text_fidelity_a:
Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White This is the best overview of the components I've seen so far:

Nexia Home Bridge (this is the key component)
Schlage touch screen deadbolt w alarm
Schlage home keypad lock
Schlage home dimmer/appliance module
Schlage home indoor camera
Schlage home outdoor camera
Trane home energy management thermostat
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) remote thermostat
Trane ComfortLink ((tm)) II Control
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) Platinum ZV control (?)
Schlage home door/window sensor
Schlage home motion sensor
Other Z-Wave sensor
Other Z-Wave thermostat
Other Z-Wave lighting device
Other Z-Wave wall switch and outlet

They might have considered making the 9V battery compartment in the "Bridge" just a little bit bigger. It's a mighty snug fit and you have to remove the battery to get the MAC ID. In fact, you have to remove the 9V battery so often it's a curiosity why the battery door is such a pain to remove and why the battery is so difficult to get out of its little bay. I was actually using a flat screwdriver to pry the battery out, it's that tight.

---

Overall, now that the camera, light dimmer and lock and installed, "enrolled" and apparently functional..? WHAT A GREAT SYSTEM!!! The components look great, they're top-quality. Now that I see everything in action (especially video of my home on my iPhone) the subscription fee seems like not such a high price to pay for what you're getting. I know that I'm going to be sorely tempted to add more cameras.

The deadbolt operates with a passcode OR with a physical key. At first I was thinking that you could lock yourself out accidentally but after examining the lock and playing with the buttons I see that is not the case.

I also understand why the light dimmer module goes so well with the indoor camera -- when it gets dark, you'd want to be able to ramp up the light enough for the camera to see! It's a temptation to put the indoor camera in one of my kids room, which is what I might have done when they were small. That would be a rude intrusion these days. So it's outside a hallway that all traffic must pass through. The field of vision nearly covers the two main doors into and out of our home, also. So I can keep an eye on who's getting home when and all that parent-of-teenagers type stuff.

Is there a controller for exterior lights? Or some kind of interface that would allow me to remotely control wired exterior lights?

The only downside to this system, aside from the kludge-y installation process, is that you will want to add more components, and they aren't cheap.

Bottom line: top-quality components, frustrating "enrollment" process -- once you get it all up and running, it's quite impressive. It's nearly worth the frustration to see it all in operation. It would be nice if you could pan-and-zoom the camera. Perhaps that will be forthcoming in another camera model.

I can't help but feel that the process of "enrolling" the components couldn't be made more simple or more streamlined.

Now to budget for an exterior camera... maybe two...

---

Now that I've seen the system in operation I grasp what the manufacturer is actually offering -- remote control of your home administered via your iPhone or iPad. Ideal for working professionals. Getting everything connected and communicating was a little effort, but it's really a beautiful system in operation. You will definitely want to add more light controls and cameras, at least I would. I wonder if there's an exterior light module? There must be. Once you see it in operation the subscription will not be an issue. You are getting more than what you're paying for.

An excellent upgrade to your home and a clever way to keep tabs on a vacation home.
text_fidelity_b: Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White

The app (Home Zone), however, is really poor. While the image appears reasonably acceptable, you can’t expand beyond a small window, at least on Apple devices. You zoom in on the center of the image but, unlike most other apps, you can’t fill the screen or even pan around the zoomed image. Further, the app is very poorly designed. It time stamps the images using 24 hour clock and non-US date structure. This cannot be changed. Not a big deal but an order of magnitude behind most competitive apps. Overall, I still find this a reasonable low cost solution. The jury is still out on the life time of the unit.

My family all pitched in and bought her a kindle for her birthday last year and I cannot express how angry I am at the customer service and quality of this product. text_fidelity_a:
Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer) These are perhaps the best in ear earphones I've ever used. They are lightweight, comfortable, stay in your ear, and offer great sound.

I've long ago ditched most earbud style earphones. They offer horrible sound, are uncomfortable, and never stay in your ear. These earphones address those issues with style, comfort, and great sound reproduction.

The mid and high range reproduction is crisp and clean without any noticeable distortion. Low range is somewhat lacking but is proberly above what most small earbud style headphones are.

They feature many great design features such as replaceable buds for the earpiece. There is small, medium, and large. There is also a set of memory foam that you can choose. This is good because as everyone's ears are different, most earpieces are not. This allows you to choose the fit of the earbuds to suit your own needs.

The part of the cable that plugs into your walkman, diskman, iPod or whatever is steel reinforced, which is nice as that is what usually breaks first on headphones. They also come with a steel carrying case to protect your headphones when not in use. They also have a cleaning tool to clean any nasty bits that may get into the canal of the phones.

All-in-all a great set of phones for the audiophile. They are lightweight, sound great, and most importantly, stay in your ear and are comfortable.
text_fidelity_b: Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) UPDATE FEB 2023 -- This is an excellent mouse. But it isn't worth $78. Similar devices are available for half that.

ORIGINAL FIVE-STAR REVIEW -- No matter what you do, a standard mouse and mouse pad become difficult to use after a time. I don't know whether the mouse surface gets worn down or the mouse pad does.

This is a vast improvement. I've been using one for a couple of years. It doesn't wear down. I'm not constantly picking the mouse up and moving it -- sometimes several times for one task. The mouse doesn't even have to be on the same surface as the computer, which adds flexibility, especially when you're using a laptop.

It's DEFINITELY better than the new generation of mouse that doesn't use batteries and has to be plugged in to charge. The plug has to go IN THE BOTTOM OF THE MOUSE, rendering it useless until it's charged. If I have work I need to get down, I don't have hours to wait for my mouse to work. Maybe someday tech people will learn the phrase "If it ain't broke, don't 'fix' it." Few things actually improve with "upgrades."
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)
